newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RTRS-HK Bank latest to raise key NZ mortgage rate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-HK Bank latest to raise key NZ mortgage rate.

text.p: Hong Kong Bank, part of the Hong Kong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Ltd, became the third New Zealand lender to raise its variable mortgage rate this week when it lifted its rate to 9.95 percent from 8.40 on Friday.
The new rate is effective immediately for new customers and from August 8 for existing customers, it said in a statement.

"Since announcing our then market-leading floating rate of 8.4 percent on May 8 the key 90-day (wholesale market) bank bill rate has risen by over 1.5 percent and we can no longer assimilate the impact of this escalation in the cost of funds," Alex Bentley, manager of personal banking, said.
"We had hoped that this present spike in interest rates would be short term. However, it looks as though it is here to stay for the foreseeable future," he added.
HK Bank joins Countrywide and ANZ who raised their mortgage rates by between 145 and 155 basis points earlier this week.

New Zealand has no core interest rate set by the central bank, only a guiding index to monetary conditions, called the MCI, which measures the composite level of the 90-day bank bill rate and the kiwi dollar's trade weighted index.
Mortgage rates therefore provide a benchmark for the retail cost of borrowing set by the commercial banks themselves.
